Pegasus · Work Centre design review · 25 September 2026

Find the work. Keep your place.

Three distinct ways to organise the office’s work, using the current Pegasus shell. Each keeps the five queue totals, Needs attention, New cases and AI jobs — with different ways to inspect and act on an item. Empty sections are omitted in all three.

Back to the v30 walkthrough
A

Priority desk

Recommended

A queue and a clear next action.

A compact work list beside a persistent detail pane. Recent arrivals and AI jobs sit below, ready when you need them.

Why choose it
The strongest balance of overview and focused casework. You can inspect each item without losing the queue.
Tradeoff
The detail pane takes some list width; supporting feeds sit further down the page.
Explore design A →
B

Office ledger

More work, easier to compare.

A full-width table makes reference, owner and due date easy to compare. Open a row to act in place; tabs switch between attention, arrivals and AI jobs.

Why choose it
Best for scanning a busy office and checking ownership across several records.
Tradeoff
New cases and AI jobs are one tab away. An expanded row temporarily makes the table taller.
Explore design B →
C

Due-date board

See the shape of the day.

Three flat lists put Overdue, Due today and Later side by side. A detail drawer opens the selected work while the board stays in place.

Why choose it
Makes the distribution of due work immediately visible, with fewer repeated group headings.
Tradeoff
Long lists need more vertical scanning. The drawer covers part of the board while you act.
Explore design C →

Recommended: A — Priority desk. It keeps the work list and the selected record together while preserving an office overview. B suits comparison across many records; C makes the day’s due groups easiest to see.
